newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Yusen, M'bishi Oil down on oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Yusen, M'bishi Oil down on oil spill.

text.p: Nippon Yusen KK and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd shares dropped in early Thursday morning trade following an oil spill in Tokyo Bay on Wednesday, brokers said.

Nippon Yusen, whose subsidiary operates the supertanker which scraped a reef and sprang a leak, was down 11 yen at 421 at 0058 GMT. Trade totalled 1.32 million shares, making it the seventh most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
Mitsubishi Oil, which chartered the tanker, was down 16 yen at 496.
Also on Thursday, Nomura Securities Co Ltd cut Nippon Yusen's ratings to a "2" rating from its previous "1".
Nomura said that the direct impact from the accident, such as the damages done to the ship and cargo and compensation for the damages, was likely to be light.
However, the accident was likely to scar the image of Japan's largest shipping firm, it said. Other costs also may increase in the aftermath of the accident.
